hook.text: A program wants to print hello on the screen. But it runs in user mode, and the screen belongs to the kernel.

ask.text: So it has to ask. That request is a system call: the program's door into the kernel.

api.text: Programs rarely knock on the door themselves. They call an A P I function, like printf in the C library, and the library makes the real system call. Here, write.

trap.text: The library puts the system call number in a register, and runs a trap instruction.

flip1.text: The mode bit flips from one to zero. We are in kernel mode.

table.text: The kernel uses the number to find the right function in the system call table.

work.text: It does the work, and leaves the result in a register.

flip2.text: Then the bit flips back to one, and the program carries on in user mode.

params.text: Parameters travel in one of three ways: in registers, in a block of memory whose address sits in a register, or pushed onto the stack.

six.text: Every system call belongs to one of six families.

six1.text: Process control, like fork and exit. File management, like open and read. Device management.

six2.text: Information maintenance, like get time. Communications, like pipe. And protection, like chmod.

mp.text: One design rule. Mechanism is how something is done. Policy is what will be done.

mp2.text: The timer is a mechanism. How long the timer is set for each user is a policy.

mp3.text: Keep them apart, and you can change the policy without rewriting the mechanism.

kern.text: So how do you build the kernel itself?

mono.text: A monolithic kernel puts everything into one big block. It is fast. But it is hard to maintain, and one bad driver can bring it all down.

micro.text: A microkernel keeps only the minimum inside. Drivers and the file system run in user space, and talk by message passing.

micro2.text: A crash stays small, so it is reliable and secure. But every message costs time.

mod.text: Linux takes a middle road: a modular kernel. A core, plus modules loaded when they are needed.

ex1.text: A system call is a controlled entry into the kernel.

ex2.text: Programs reach it through an A P I.

ex4.text: Mechanism is how, policy is what.

ex5.text: Monolithic is fast, microkernel is safe.
